topics.label: Imperative Programming
topics.desc: Computation expressed as explicit sequences of statements mutating program state, the model underlying most mainstream languages and CPUs.

topics.label: Procedural Programming
topics.desc: Structuring imperative code into reusable procedures with call stacks and local scope, the basis of C-style modular decomposition.

topics.label: Object-Oriented Programming
topics.desc: Organizing programs as interacting objects bundling state and behavior via encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism for modeling domains.

topics.label: Functional Programming
topics.desc: Building programs from pure functions and immutable data, emphasizing composition and referential transparency over mutable state.

topics.label: Declarative Programming
topics.desc: Specifying what result is wanted rather than how to compute it, letting the runtime determine control flow, as in SQL or logic languages.

topics.label: Logic Programming
topics.desc: Expressing computation as logical relations and rules resolved by unification and backtracking, exemplified by Prolog and constraint solvers.

topics.label: Reactive Programming
topics.desc: Modeling computation as propagation of change through declarative data-flow streams, automatically updating dependents when inputs change.

topics.label: Array Programming
topics.desc: Operating on whole arrays as primitive values with vectorized operations, central to APL/J and numerical computing like NumPy.

topics.label: Static vs Dynamic Typing
topics.desc: The fundamental tradeoff between checking types at compile time versus at runtime, shaping safety, tooling, and developer flexibility.

topics.label: Strong vs Weak Typing
topics.desc: How strictly a language enforces type boundaries and resists implicit coercions, affecting how easily type errors silently propagate.

topics.label: Type Inference
topics.desc: Automatically deducing expression types without annotations, typically via Hindley-Milner unification, giving static safety with terse code.

topics.label: Algebraic Data Types
topics.desc: Composite types built from sums (tagged unions) and products (records) enabling exhaustive pattern matching and precise domain modeling.

topics.label: Parametric Polymorphism
topics.desc: Code abstracted uniformly over type parameters (generics), enabling reuse with full static type safety across instantiations.

topics.label: Subtyping & Variance
topics.desc: Rules governing when one type substitutes for another, including covariance and contravariance of generic and function types.

topics.label: Type Classes & Traits
topics.desc: Ad-hoc polymorphism via constraint-based interfaces resolved at compile time, as in Haskell type classes and Rust traits.

topics.label: Dependent & Refinement Types
topics.desc: Types parameterized by values, letting the type system encode and verify rich invariants and proofs, as in Idris and Agda.

topics.label: Gradual Typing
topics.desc: Mixing static and dynamic typing within one program via optional annotations, enabling incremental migration as in TypeScript and mypy.

topics.label: Syntax & Grammar
topics.desc: The formal surface structure of a language, typically specified by context-free grammars in BNF that define well-formed programs.

topics.label: Lexical vs Dynamic Scope
topics.desc: How identifier bindings resolve—by textual nesting versus call-stack context—a core decision affecting closures and reasoning.

topics.label: Evaluation Strategies
topics.desc: Rules for when and how arguments are evaluated, including call-by-value, call-by-reference, and lazy call-by-need.

topics.label: Operational Semantics
topics.desc: Defining program meaning as state-transition rules of an abstract machine, the standard tool for specifying language behavior precisely.

topics.label: Denotational Semantics
topics.desc: Assigning mathematical objects (functions over domains) as the meaning of programs, abstracting away execution details.

topics.label: Lambda Calculus
topics.desc: The minimal formal model of computation by function abstraction and application, the theoretical foundation of functional languages.

topics.label: Binding & Environments
topics.desc: How names map to values through environment frames, underpinning variable resolution, closures, and substitution semantics.

topics.label: Undefined Behavior
topics.desc: Program constructs whose semantics the spec leaves unconstrained, permitting aggressive optimization but enabling subtle, unsafe bugs.

topics.label: Manual Memory Management
topics.desc: Explicit allocation and deallocation by the programmer, offering control at the cost of leaks, double-frees, and dangling pointers.

topics.label: Stack vs Heap
topics.desc: The distinction between automatic LIFO stack storage and dynamically managed heap allocation, governing object lifetime and cost.

topics.label: Garbage Collection
topics.desc: Automatic reclamation of unreachable memory via tracing or reference counting, trading runtime overhead and pauses for safety.

topics.label: Reference Counting
topics.desc: Reclaiming objects when their reference count hits zero, giving deterministic destruction but failing on reference cycles.

topics.label: Ownership & Borrowing
topics.desc: Compile-time memory discipline tracking unique ownership and borrows, giving safety without GC as pioneered by Rust.

topics.label: RAII & Deterministic Cleanup
topics.desc: Tying resource lifetime to object scope so destructors release memory, locks, and handles deterministically, central to C++.

topics.label: Smart Pointers
topics.desc: Wrapper types encoding ownership semantics (unique, shared, weak) to automate deallocation and prevent common pointer errors.

topics.label: Memory Safety
topics.desc: The property of preventing invalid memory access—buffer overruns, use-after-free—through language design or runtime checks.

topics.label: Value vs Reference Semantics
topics.desc: Whether assignment copies data or shares a reference, determining aliasing behavior, mutation visibility, and equality.

topics.label: First-Class Functions
topics.desc: Treating functions as ordinary values that can be passed, returned, and stored, the basis of higher-order abstraction.

topics.label: Closures
topics.desc: Functions capturing their lexical environment so they retain access to enclosing variables after that scope returns.

topics.label: Pattern Matching
topics.desc: Destructuring and dispatching on the shape of data with exhaustiveness checking, a concise alternative to nested conditionals.

topics.label: Exception Handling
topics.desc: Structured nonlocal control flow for propagating and recovering from errors via throw/catch and stack unwinding.

topics.label: Iterators & Generators
topics.desc: Abstractions for lazy sequential traversal, with generators suspending and resuming execution to yield values on demand.

topics.label: Coroutines & Async/Await
topics.desc: Cooperatively suspendable functions enabling readable asynchronous and concurrent code without explicit callback nesting.

topics.label: Operator Overloading
topics.desc: Defining custom behavior for built-in operators on user types, improving expressiveness for numeric and DSL-like APIs.

topics.label: Immutability & Persistent Data
topics.desc: Data that cannot change after creation, enabling safe sharing, easy reasoning, and efficient structural-sharing collections.

topics.label: Macros & Code Generation
topics.desc: Programmatically generating or transforming source before compilation, from C text macros to hygienic and procedural systems.

topics.label: Homoiconicity & Lisp Macros
topics.desc: Languages where code is represented as manipulable data structures, enabling uniquely powerful syntactic macros as in Lisp.

topics.label: Reflection
topics.desc: A program inspecting and modifying its own structure—types, fields, methods—at runtime, powering frameworks and serializers.

topics.label: Annotations & Attributes
topics.desc: Declarative metadata attached to code elements that tools and runtimes consume to drive behavior like DI, ORM, and validation.

topics.label: Compile-Time Metaprogramming
topics.desc: Computation executed during compilation—templates, constexpr, comptime, derive macros—to generate code with zero runtime cost.

topics.label: Domain-Specific Languages
topics.desc: Specialized mini-languages, embedded or standalone, that express solutions in a domain's own vocabulary for clarity and safety.

topics.label: Aspect-Oriented Programming
topics.desc: Modularizing cross-cutting concerns like logging and transactions by weaving advice into join points across a codebase.

topics.label: Dynamic Evaluation
topics.desc: Runtime construction and execution of code via eval or quasi-quotation, offering flexibility at a cost to safety and performance.

topics.label: Compiled vs Interpreted
topics.desc: The spectrum from ahead-of-time native compilation to tree-walking interpretation, trading startup, portability, and peak speed.

topics.label: Bytecode Virtual Machines
topics.desc: Compiling to portable bytecode executed by a VM like the JVM or CLR, balancing portability with optimizable intermediate code.

topics.label: JIT Compilation
topics.desc: Compiling hot code to native instructions at runtime using profiling and speculation to approach static-compilation speed.

topics.label: Managed Runtimes
topics.desc: Execution environments providing GC, type safety, and reflection over raw hardware, abstracting platform details for the program.

topics.label: Foreign Function Interface
topics.desc: Mechanisms for calling across language boundaries, bridging managed code to native libraries with marshaling and ABI concerns.

topics.label: Concurrency Execution Models
topics.desc: How a runtime schedules concurrent work—OS threads, green threads, event loops, or actors—shaping the language's concurrency story.

topics.label: Abstract Machines
topics.desc: Idealized execution engines like the SECD or Warren machine that bridge high-level semantics to concrete implementation.

topics.label: WebAssembly & Portable Targets
topics.desc: A portable, sandboxed bytecode target enabling near-native execution of many languages across browsers and edge runtimes.

topics.label: C-Family Languages
topics.desc: Systems languages descended from C (C++, Objective-C) prioritizing low-level control, manual memory, and zero-cost abstractions.

topics.label: ML-Family Languages
topics.desc: Statically typed functional languages (OCaml, Haskell, F#) defined by type inference, ADTs, and pattern matching.

topics.label: Lisp-Family Languages
topics.desc: S-expression languages (Scheme, Clojure, Common Lisp) known for homoiconicity, macros, and dynamic interactive development.

topics.label: JVM Languages
topics.desc: Languages targeting the JVM (Java, Kotlin, Scala, Clojure) sharing its runtime, GC, and vast interoperable ecosystem.

topics.label: Dynamic Scripting Languages
topics.desc: Dynamically typed, rapid-development languages (Python, Ruby, JavaScript) favoring expressiveness and fast iteration.

topics.label: Modern Systems Languages
topics.desc: Newer low-level languages (Rust, Go, Zig) combining performance and safety with modern tooling and concurrency models.

topics.label: Idioms & Conventions
topics.desc: Community-established patterns and idiomatic usage that make code natural within a language, beyond mere syntactic correctness.

topics.label: Imperative-Procedural Link
topics.desc: Procedural style refines raw imperative computation with named procedures and structured control over shared mutable state.

topics.label: Multiparadigm Languages
topics.desc: Languages deliberately blending paradigms so developers mix object-oriented, functional, and imperative styles within one program.
